personas.name: B-E DEv
personas.reaction: One more MCP server in every session sounds like fluff to me, unless it costs nothing until my agent actually needs a rule.

personas.name: F-E Developer
personas.reaction: If the runner's agents read the real rules before they decide, there is less slop for me to catch in review.

personas.name: Paul - Product Manager
personas.reaction: Every runner I send a PRD to knows the product's laws with no setup: that is what lets me ship across repositories.

personas.name: Lead Engineer
personas.reaction: Every agent on the team, not only the ones whose owner pasted a key, reads the same ADRs: that is the cohesion I want.

personas.name: Irisa
personas.reaction: Nothing to paste for my mobile team: if I am signed in, it works.

objection.text: One more MCP server in every session sounds like fluff to me. If it slows my session or answers junk, I will switch it off.

rounds.fit: Fits the PM, the lead engineer and Irisa best, and the skeptical back-end developer worst, until the server was made silent before its first call.

personas.name: B-E DEv
personas.reaction: Silent until called, one line when it fails, and the ids cited: I can check it is not fluff.

personas.name: F-E Developer
personas.reaction: Outbox items that cite the rule they followed are something I can review instead of guessing.

personas.name: Paul - Product Manager
personas.reaction: Runners on fixed skills finally read the product's knowledge with their own token.

personas.name: Lead Engineer
personas.reaction: One switch stops every agent, keys and sign-ins alike: I keep control.

personas.name: Irisa
personas.reaction: No key to make and no line to paste: it is just there.

rounds.fit: Fits every persona at 3 or more; the skeptical back-end developer waits to see that it stays silent until used.
